MCP Console gives your MCP client one tool, `send`, for running R, Python, and SQL.
Data, models, imports, and database state stay available between calls.
Results include text and plots, with complete logs and artifacts saved on disk.

::: {.home-links}
[Get started](getting-started.qmd){.btn .btn-primary} [Read the docs](README.md){.btn .btn-outline-primary}
:::

## Work across languages

With both runtimes available, Python reads R objects through `r.name`, R reads Python objects through `py$name`, and SQL can query live R data frames.
Python and SQL also work without R.

```r
measurements <- data.frame(value = c(2, 4, 6))
mean(measurements$value)
```

In a later Python call, the R object is still available:

```python
r.measurements
```

Sessions support interactive input, dependency preparation, interruption, and restart.
The [runtime guide](BUILTIN_RUNTIME.md) describes language bridges, SQL connections, and plots.

## Status and execution

MCP Console is a **development preview**; interfaces may change.
macOS and Linux are supported, and Windows x64 has [experimental local support](WINDOWS.md).

Console runs processes on the host where it is launched.
Evaluated code has shell-class capability.
The default [native sandbox](SANDBOX.md) restricts writes and direct networking, but permits host-file reads, including readable secrets.
[Dependency preparation](REQUIREMENTS.md#host-resolution-and-trust) is a separate trusted host operation.
